deck.title: Warm & Fuzzies — SUEDE Designathon 2026 pitch draft
deck.narrative_rule: Move from unprompted appreciation to a working social-script hypothesis, the evidence gap, the need-state audience, one explicit design brief, one solution sentence and one shared live demo.
deck.evidence_rule: The displayed participant ratings and percentages are disclosed in the slide footers as temporary rehearsal data because Ethan explicitly requested presentable test values; they must be replaced before the judged pitch. Published studies support only the adjacent channel mechanisms, not the practice values, plotted positions, Goldilocks gap or product superiority.

design.direction: Warm & Fuzzies paper-and-ink presentation system derived from Cecelia's current brand board
design.signature: An unprompted-appreciation question becomes an occasion rule, a visibly unproven format gap, an evidence-to-solution deduction and one shared live giving ritual.

slides.audience_takeaway: Meet the product identity and team, then move immediately.

visual.composition: Cecelia's firefly and the Warm & Fuzzies wordmark on white, with the approved team name, team number and confirmed member names. Do not add narrative copy.

speaker_notes: Timing: 5 seconds.
Name the team and move.
Blocked until team number and member-name spelling are confirmed.

motion.description: Reveal the human-drawn identity once; no ambient loop.

slides.claim: When was the last time you showed someone appreciation or gratitude?
slides.audience_takeaway: Recall the last time they initiated an unprompted act of appreciation before the team names the problem.

visual.composition: One full-frame question ending with `appreciation or gratitude?` Do not put the birthday or event clarification on the slide. Do not mention letters, because that reveals a solution format before the problem is established. No counterpoint, supporting sentence or raise-hands prompt.

speaker_notes: Timing: 20 seconds.
Ask the visible sender-framed appreciation-or-gratitude question and pause briefly. Then say aloud that birthdays, celebrations and major events do not count.
Do not mention letters, ask for raised hands or add the removed `we have never had more ways to talk` counterpoint.
A pause or difficulty remembering opens the story; it is not evidence.
Cultural transmission and fear of social judgment remain mechanisms to research, not facts to state.

motion.description: One question appears once; no staged subtext.

slides.claim: We appreciate our friends and family. We just do not always show it.
slides.audience_takeaway: Understand the problem as an expression barrier, not missing care.

visual.composition: One plain problem statement in the established navy-and-white colour system. No Chloe attribution, mentor quote, persona, explanatory paragraph or orange detour.

speaker_notes: Timing: 15 seconds.
Say that appreciation can already exist while expressing it on an ordinary day still feels out of the ordinary.
Treat this as the team's current problem framing, not a prevalence finding.

motion.description: Emphasise `show it` only after the full statement lands.

slides.claim: Care this explicit can feel like it needs a reason.
slides.audience_takeaway: Understand the working social script and why ordinary-day appreciation is worth testing.

visual.composition: A connected birthday, farewell and milestone cluster represents ready-made social scripts. A visual break isolates an ordinary Tuesday with no ready-made script. The slide cites the adjacent sender-miscalibration and non-occasion-gift evidence, then asks how ordinary-day appreciation could become easier to send.

speaker_notes: Timing: 20 seconds.

Say: `Milestones give us a script. On an ordinary Tuesday, we suspected that script disappears and people hold back. That is our hypothesis. Research shows senders often overestimate awkwardness, while spontaneous care can be welcome. So how might we make ordinary-day appreciation easier to send?`

Kumar and Epley studied gratitude letters; Givi and Galak studied anticipated reactions to non-occasion gifts. They justify testing the social script but do not prove an occasion rule, crisis interpretation or prevalence rate.

motion.description: Show occasion prompts, then the unprompted ordinary day, then the How Might We.

slides.claim: The possible Goldilocks gap combines high recipient impact, low mental and physical friction, and enough frequency for an ordinary day.
slides.audience_takeaway: See three psychology-informed mechanism cues across the broad form families and the combination the team is trying to reach, without turning the pitch into a literature review.

visual.composition: An impact-versus-friction map where each clearly visible circle behind a channel icon encodes how frequently that form family is received. Hand-drawn channel icons distinguish quick text, voice note / video call and handwritten letter / physical gift. Each reveal keeps one large, bounded psychological mechanism and author-year citation: tone can be misread; voice can feel closer; thoughtfulness matters more than price. Keep numeric ratings for page 6. Finish on an unboxed `goldilocks zone`, marked by Cecelia's firefly mascot in the same deep navy as the deck typography, for high impact, low friction and repeatability. The high-contrast axes and footer keep the three encodings and evidence boundary explicit.

speaker_notes: Timing: 25 seconds.

Say: `We pressure-tested this map against psychology: text can lose tone, voice can feel more connecting, and thoughtfulness—not price—is what helps care land. So we are testing a Goldilocks space that keeps expression easy but makes care more legible and worth keeping.`
Do not explain paper methods unless asked in Q&A; the visible author-year citations establish the trail.
The papers support only the mechanism labels, not the map positions, grouped-channel equivalence or the Goldilocks target.
Replace every grouped position, point size and all temporary figures on slides 6 and 8 with documented results before the judged pitch.

motion.description: Reveal the three channel families with their unboxed paper conclusions, then reveal the Goldilocks combination on the fourth click.

slides.claim: 82% feel they do not fully show their appreciation; 71% say ordinary-day appreciation can feel awkward or out of place; the channel families each trade impact, friction and frequency.
slides.audience_takeaway: Read the headline figures and channel comparison immediately, without first parsing three research questions.

visual.composition: Remove the visible What / Why / How labels, questions and decorative rules. Treat 82% and its one-line meaning, then 71% and its one-line meaning, as two continuous headline blocks. Use a hand-drawn three-row trade-off ledger with one shared metric header, large channel icons and large values so it reads as one editorial field note rather than a miniature dashboard. On a fourth click, circle letter/gift impact, quick-text friction and voice/video frequency to show the three qualities the team wants to combine. A footer discloses that all grouped figures are temporary and do not establish equivalence.

speaker_notes: Timing: 40 seconds.
Reveal the 82% and 71% findings directly, then reveal the three grouped form families and explain that each has strengths but no family captures all three.
Click once more to circle the three source qualities: letter/gift impact, text friction and voice/video frequency.
Every value is temporary rehearsal data. Replace it after recruitment, method, sample, wording, analysis, exact results, exceptions and limitations are recorded.
Psychology on text meaningfulness, synchronous voice/video and perceived effort supports only the channel mechanisms; it cannot validate these grouped figures or equivalence.

motion.description: Reveal the two headline findings and the compact channel ledger, then circle the three qualities the solution will combine.

slides.audience_takeaway: Understand the first target as people whose desired gesture falls between an ordinary text and a physical letter or gift.

visual.composition: Use two oversized cropped Goldilocks rings to divide the full 1600 by 900 canvas into three vertical bands. Reduce the left band to `text — too awkward or too casual` and the right to `letter / gift — too much; high friction; inaccessible`. The centre has one emotional hierarchy: `They care. But appreciation stays unspoken.`, followed by university students, long-distance connections, close friends and close family as quiet included examples rather than exclusive demographics or validated segments.

speaker_notes: Timing: 20 seconds.
Reveal the text-side constraint, then the letter-or-gift constraint, then the people caught in between.
Define the target by the situation: they already care, but neither existing format fits the ordinary moment, so the appreciation can stay unspoken.
Use university students, long-distance connections, close friends and close family as included examples only.
This remains a working need-state, not validated demand, market size or a research-derived persona.

motion.description: Reveal the left oversized ring and text constraint, then the right oversized ring and physical-gesture constraint, then the audience and consequence in the band between them.

slides.claim: If the expression gap exists and ordinary-day appreciation feels awkward, then normalise the act by aiming for gift-level impact with digital-level friction and repeatability.
slides.audience_takeaway: Follow the evidence deduction into one explicit product requirement before the solution reveal.

visual.composition: Preserve the high-contrast If / And / Then chain. Add a fourth unboxed `Therefore` line at the bottom: create the impact of gift-giving with the low friction and repeatability of everyday digital contact. Use the same temporary 82% and 71% rehearsal figures as slide 6, disclosed in the footer, until real results replace them.

speaker_notes: Timing: 15 seconds.
For rehearsal, connect the temporary What and Why figures, name normalising ordinary-day appreciation as the outcome, then state the product requirement in the Therefore line.
Replace the two temporary percentages before the judged pitch. The desired outcome and Goldilocks combination remain a design deduction, not a validated result.

motion.description: Reveal If, And, Then and the added Therefore requirement in order.

slides.claim: Warm & Fuzzies is a private digital keepsake that brings the thoughtfulness of a letter to the ease of a text.
slides.audience_takeaway: Understand the proposed solution and intended comparative advantage in one sentence before the live demonstration.

visual.composition: One large centred sentence only: `Warm & Fuzzies is a private digital keepsake that brings the thoughtfulness of a letter to the ease of a text.` Emphasise the two borrowed qualities in the blue accent. Remove the phone screenshot, product-name lockup, mechanism subtext and prototype footer.

speaker_notes: Timing: 20 seconds.
Read or closely paraphrase the single solution sentence, then switch immediately to the running prototype.
Treat thoughtfulness plus ease as the product proposition that the demo makes legible, not as a validated superiority claim or measured outcome.

motion.description: Show the complete solution sentence at once, then stop deck motion for the live demo.

slides.audience_takeaway: Open the public demo by QR while watching one complete working sender-to-receiver journey rather than a narrated feature tour.

visual.composition: A dark live-demo handoff with `Follow along.` on the left and a large verified QR for `https://warm-and-fuzzies.vercel.app/demo` on the right. Include the readable short URL and a no-phone instruction. No screenshots, process checklist or second closing slide.

speaker_notes: Timing: 100 seconds.
Invite the room to scan the public demo if they want to follow on their own phone, then switch to the live prototype.
Show only the critical path: compose one object, seal it, choose its travel, create the link, open as receiver, then keep, close or remove without replying.

Explain the relevant process decision while it appears: why the object shows effort, why sealing creates closure, why the link reduces receiving friction and why the receiver controls the ending. Keep the emphasis on the research logic, not a separate process diary.
Demonstrate only working states. Do not claim delivery infrastructure, verified identity, encrypted privacy, ownership, permanent storage or lower awkwardness.
The public QR is a generic demo route, not a personalised thank-you, participant task or validation event.

motion.description: Show the QR once, then stop deck motion while the presenter demonstrates the working prototype.
